'''William L. Kruer''' (born 20 April 1942, [[Louisville, Kentucky|Louisville]], [[Kentucky]]) is an American physicist, specializing in [[plasma physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11604004.html|title=Kruer, William L.|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref>

Kruer studied at the [[University of Louisville]] (Master's degree, 1965) and received his Ph.D. in 1969 from [[Princeton University]]. Afterwards, he was a research associate scientist at the [[Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory]] and from 1970 a full member of the research staff. Starting in 1972, he was a group leader for theoretical plasma physics and simulation at [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] and from 1993 a chief scientist in plasma physics there. He wrote an important book on laser plasma interactions.<ref>{{cite book|author=Kruer, William L.|title=The Physics of Laser Plasma Interactions|year=2001|publisher=Westview Press|isbn=9780813340838|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uAF_HWb8FAQC}}</ref>

In 1990, he received the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Kruer&first_nm=William&year=1990|title=1990 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|last=|first=|date=|website=American Physical Society|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref>
